description: Per-document-type default template picker (Invoice/Credit Note, Estimate/Quotation, Delivery Challan, Purchase Invoice, Payment In/Out) for the full-page A4 bill used for WhatsApp PDF sharing and formal printing.
what_it_does: Lets the shop choose which A4 layout is used by default for each kind of document when it is shared as a PDF or printed on a normal printer, mirroring the Thermal Invoice Library but for the A4 format and across more document types.
current_behavior: The 'Document Type' dropdown correctly switches doctype and loads the right existing Print Format (Sales Invoice, Quotation, Delivery Note, Payment Entry all have real formats). Purchase Invoice currently shows 'no document to preview' because this shop has not created a real purchase bill yet -- not a bug, just no data. 'Set as Default' posts to Santu Document Template Settings, a per-(library, document type) child table that did not exist as a real table until 2026-08-29 (clicking the button crashed with a SQL error before that) -- now fixed and verified end to end.
expected_behavior: Every document type should have at least one A4 template selectable, and picking a default should actually change what prints/shares -- today only Sales Invoice's A4 default is wired into the actual print/WhatsApp send path; the other document types' Set as Default currently only saves the setting without yet being read back by their own print/send functions.
how_it_works: Printer Settings > A4/WhatsApp Library section -> pick Document Type -> pick a template -> preview loads -> Set as Default saves a row per document type.
how_to_use:
1. Utilities > Printer Settings > scroll to A4/WhatsApp Library.
2. Pick the Document Type from the dropdown.
3. Click a template to preview, then Set as Default.
qa_testing:
Verified: dropdown switches doctype and preview correctly for Sales Invoice, Quotation, Delivery Note, Payment Entry. Purchase Invoice correctly shows the 'no document yet' message instead of an error.
Not yet verified: whether Quotation/Delivery Note/Payment Entry's actual print/send functions read this saved default the way Sales Invoice's thermal path does -- flagged Partial until traced.
related_features: Thermal Invoice Library, WhatsApp Connect, Estimate/Quotation, Delivery Challan
if_we_modify:
Data impact: Santu Document Template Settings child table -- confirm library string values here always match the JS library keys exactly (Data field, not Select, specifically to avoid this drifting).
Printing impact: only Sales Invoice is confirmed to actually change behavior when its default changes; treat the other four document types as read-the-setting-but-verify-it-is-used before relying on them.

description: Counter-side quick sale screen -- the actual screen the cashier bills from.
what_it_does: Scan or search items, adjust qty/rate/discount per row, pick payment mode, save and print in one screen. Multiple bills can stay open as tabs.
current_behavior: Each line is a plain object in memory (santu_billing.js). Rows can be deleted with the ✕ button per row or F4 on the selected row. F6 opens Change Unit if the item has more than one UOM. Saving posts a real Sales Invoice via santu_hardware.api.save_sale_invoice, which is_pos=1 for cash and plain credit for udhaar. Thermal print goes through print_service.print_via_cups using whichever template is set as default in Printer Settings.
expected_behavior: A cashier should never need the keyboard or mouse for anything but scanning and typing amounts. Every F-key shortcut (F1 search, F2 qty, F3 discount, F4 remove, F5 rate, F6 unit, F7 rename, F8 charges, F9 bill discount, F11 customer, F12 remarks) must work without touching the item row first if a row is already selected.
how_it_works: Scan/search item -> row added -> adjust qty/rate/discount -> pick customer (optional for cash) -> pick payment mode -> Save & Print -> Sales Invoice created and submitted -> stock deducted -> thermal bill sent to printer or WhatsApp.
how_to_use:
1. Type or scan item code in the search box.
2. Item row appears; click +/- or press F2 to change qty.
3. Optionally search customer (F11) for udhaar/khata sale.
4. Pick Payment Mode -- Cash marks is_pos=1 and auto-fills Amount Received.
5. Press Save & Print (Ctrl+P) or Save & Print Only.
6. Bill number and stock update immediately; thermal print or WhatsApp share follows.
qa_testing:
Normal: 1 item cash sale, multiple items, udhaar sale.
Edge: 100+ line items (tested 2026-08-29, all render correctly on thermal + A4), long item names (must wrap not clip), zero-qty row (blocked), deleting the only row, changing customer mid-bill, unit change with different UOM conversion factor (rate/qty must rescale).
Failure cases: credit sale to a customer over their credit limit must be blocked with the exact shortfall shown; credit sale to a customer with no phone/address must be blocked.
Regression risk: any change here can silently affect stock (Bin), GL entries, and the customer's outstanding balance -- always re-run a full sale + return + partial-payment cycle after editing.
related_features: Items, Stock, Customer Ledger, Payment In, Thermal Invoice Library, A4/WhatsApp Library, Credit Limit
if_we_modify:
UI impact: cashier muscle memory (F-keys) breaks if shortcuts move.
Data impact: Sales Invoice, Sales Invoice Item, Payment Entry rows.
Stock impact: every saved row posts a Stock Ledger Entry immediately on submit.
Ledger impact: GL entries post on submit; a bad edit can leave GL unbalanced.
Printing impact: whichever template is default in Printer Settings prints automatically -- verify the chosen template still renders 100% of items.
Related: Return screens read `sales_invoice_item` back-references from here; breaking the item id here breaks returns.
Regression testing required: yes, full core-sale + returns-payments suite.

description: POS Billing is the single place a bill is made. The second billing screen (Sale Invoices, route santu-sale-invoice) has been retired.
what_it_does: All billing happens on POS Billing (santu-billing). The old second billing screen is gone; its route now forwards there, so old bookmarks and links still land somewhere useful.
current_behavior:
Everything the retired screen could do and Billing could not was moved into Billing first: draft save (save without submitting), Terms & Conditions, customer note, photo/document attachments, the unprinted-bills alert with 'Dobara chhapo', and 'kuch gadbad hai' reporting. They sit behind the 'More' button next to Save.

Deliberately NOT ported: the Round Off checkbox. Round-off is what produced the phantom 50-paise 'due' on a fully-paid bill (28-08-2026); disable_rounded_total is pinned to 1 on every bill on purpose.
how_it_works:
santu_hardware/santu_hardware/page/santu_billing/ is the only billing screen. page/santu_sale_invoice/santu_sale_invoice.js is now a 25-line redirect stub.

IMPORTANT: public/js/santu_sale_invoice/santu_sale_invoice_api.js is NOT part of the removed screen despite the matching name. It is the SHARED library -- Estimate, Sales Order, Delivery Challan, Sales Return, Payment Entry, Party Transfer and Billing itself all call it. Deleting it would break seven screens.
how_to_use:
Bill banane ke liye sirf Billing (POS) kholein.
More button (Save ke bagal me):
  - Draft save karo: bill save hoga par submit nahi -- na stock hilega, na khata. Baad me poora kar sakte hain.
  - Terms & Conditions: bill ke neeche chhapne wali baat.
  - Customer ka note: ghar/landmark, customer par bhi save hota hai.
  - Photo / Document lagao: pehle draft save karein, phir file lagayein.
  - Kuch gadbad hai? Batao: jo hua waisa likh dein, record ho jayega.
Upar peeli patti aaye to matlab koi bill chhapa nahi -- 'Dobara chhapo' dabayein.
qa_testing:
Automated: scratchpad/qa/batch_pos.py -- 18 scenarios (draft posts nothing, draft->submit moves stock, terms/remarks stored, no phantom paise, full unit list, selling in an alternate unit, reopened rows, disabled item, line/bill discount, credit baaki, partial payment, stock moves once, multi-line, empty bill refused). Last run: 18/18.
Regression: batch1 217/217, batch2 36/36, batch3 390/390.
Manual: open /app/santu-sale-invoice -- it must land on Billing, not an empty page.
related_features: Change Unit everywhere; Edit Submitted Documents
if_we_modify:
Never re-create a second billing screen. Two screens meant two item tables, two save paths and two unit-conversion implementations, and they disagreed -- on 30-08-2026 both were found mis-scaling a unit change in DIFFERENT ways. Desk is a single-page app, so two page scripts in one session also share a global scope: a top-level `const` of the same name in both is a SyntaxError that blanks the second screen.

If a billing capability is missing, add it to POS Billing. If the old screen is ever needed for reference, it is in git (commit 3a1cd73) and at scratchpad/santu_sale_invoice.js.removed_backup.

description: Any item can be billed, purchased, returned or stocked in any unit, from every screen, with rate and quantity rescaling together.
what_it_does: One shared helper (public/js/santu_uom.js) gives every screen the same unit list and the same conversion maths. Stock Summary can also change an item's unit outright.
current_behavior:
Stock Summary: tap the unit next to the quantity. An item with no history switches its stock unit; an item with history keeps its stock unit and gains the new one as an alternate (1 Gram = 0.001 Kg is worked out automatically). Stock is never silently reinterpreted.

Billing / Estimate / Sales Return / Purchase Return: F6.
Sale Invoice list screens, Purchase Invoice, Sales Order, Purchase Order, Delivery Challan: the unit dropdown in the row.
how_it_works:
santu_uom.list()/prime() read santu_hardware.santu_hardware.api.item_uoms / items_uoms -- the item's own units first, then every unit in the system, with shop-common ones (Nos, Kg, Gram, Litre, Meter, Box...) ahead of the rest of the ~250.

santu_uom.convert() moves the two halves in OPPOSITE directions: quantity and stock scale by old/new, rate scales by new/old, so qty x rate -- what the customer pays -- never moves.

Backend: _conversion_factor_for() resolves the factor on every save path from the item's own UOM table when the caller does not send one.
how_to_use:
Stock Summary me item ke bagal wali unit (jaise 'Kg') par dabayein -> naya unit chunein. Agar system khud samajh sakta hai (Gram/Kg, Litre/ml, Meter/cm) to factor apne aap bharega, warna aapse poochega ki 1 naya unit me kitne purane hote hain.
Bill banate waqt row chunkar F6 -> unit badal dein. Rate aur quantity dono apne aap adjust honge, bill ka total wahi rahega.
qa_testing:
batch_pos.py: 'Selling in an alternate unit bills and stocks correctly' -- 500 g of a Kg item at 0.25/g must bill 125 and take 0.5 Kg off the shelf.
Live check: add an item on Billing, F6 to Gram, save as draft, open the Sales Invoice -- stock_qty must be in the STOCK unit (1 Kg for 1000 g), not the typed number.
if_we_modify:
Never let a screen build its own unit list again. Five screens each built [row.uom, row.stock_uom] in the browser, which is why a Kg item offered only 'Kg' and could not be billed in grams (30-08-2026).

Never assume conversion_factor = 1 for a unit that is not the stock unit. That is what made 500 grams take 500 KILOGRAMS off the shelf -- the screen sent the unit but no factor, and the server defaulted to 1. _conversion_factor_for() now guards every save path; keep new save paths going through it.

description: Creates a new customer profile.
what_it_does: Maintains customer details including name, phone number, address, and opening balance.
current_behavior: Creates a standard Frappe Customer record and an associated Contact record for WhatsApp.
expected_behavior: Should quickly onboard a new customer during checkout or independently.
how_it_works: Enter Name & Phone -> Save -> Customer + Contact created -> Accessible in Sales POS.
how_to_use:
1. Dashboard -> Add Customer (or from Sale POS)
2. Enter details
3. Save
qa_testing:
**Test Cases:**
- Duplicate phone number
- Missing name
- Creating customer during live sale checkout.
if_we_modify:
**Impact Areas:**
- Contact linking for WhatsApp.
- Customer selection dropdowns in Sales.

description: The party box on the Billing (POS) screen -- browse every customer by scrolling, or narrow the list by typing a name or a phone number.
what_it_does: Lets the cashier attach a sale to the right existing customer instead of creating a near-duplicate, whether or not they remember how the name is spelled.
current_behavior: list_customers_for_picker() backs the box. An empty query lists every customer, most recently dealt-with first (today's customers near the top), and the dropdown scrolls. A typed query matches name OR phone in one call, with names that START with the query ranked first. Previously the box needed at least 2 characters and returned nothing at all when empty -- clicking in offered only 'Add Customer', so a cashier who could not recall the spelling had no way to reach an existing regular and would create a duplicate (2026-08-29 direct request).
expected_behavior: Clicking the empty party box should show everyone; typing should narrow it; both should be reachable without knowing exact spelling.
how_it_works: Click/focus party box -> full customer list loads (name + phone, scrollable) -> type to narrow by name or phone -> click a row to attach that customer to the bill. 'Add Customer' stays available at the bottom regardless of results.
how_to_use:
1. In Billing (POS), click the customer box (or press F11).
2. Scroll the list to find the customer, or type part of their name or phone number.
3. Click their row. If they are genuinely new, use 'Add Customer' (Ctrl+D).
qa_testing:
Verified 2026-08-29 in the live screen: empty box listed all 7 customers with phone numbers; typing a partial phone ('62066') narrowed to the right customer; typing a name matched too; dropdown measured scrollable (content 375px inside a 318px box, overflow-y auto) so a long customer list stays reachable.
Edge cases to re-check as the shop grows: several hundred customers (the API caps at 200 -- revisit if the shop passes that), and customers with no phone on file (shown as an em dash, not blank).
related_features: Billing (POS), Customer Creation, Payment In / Credit Limit
if_we_modify:
UI impact: the dropdown's scroll depends on its max-height plus overflow-y -- removing either makes long lists unreachable again.
Data impact: none, read-only.
Business logic impact: this is the main defence against duplicate customers, which in turn keeps khata balances correct -- a regression here shows up later as split balances across two records of the same person.
Regression testing required: check the empty-box case specifically; it is the one that was broken and the one nobody thinks to test.

description: Adjustable sliders for logo sizes in A4 and Thermal bills.
what_it_does: Allows manual control over the exact mm/% size of the shop logo separately for thermal receipts and A4 invoices from the Invoice Settings page.
how_to_use: Go to Invoice Settings > Logo Library. Use the slider below the A4 or Thermal logo to set the size. A live preview shows the exact proportion before you print.

description: Reopen and correct an already-submitted document -- add items, change qty/rate, fix a wrong entry -- without losing the number the customer already has.
what_it_does: Cancels the original and rebuilds it through that screen's own save path, chained via amended_from, so a correction is identical in every way to a document created fresh.
current_behavior:
Backend (edit_submitted_document + get_document_for_edit) supports Quotation, Sales Order, Delivery Note, Purchase Invoice and Purchase Order -- all five verified end to end. Sales Invoice keeps its own older, payment-aware path (edit_submitted_sale_invoice) because it must also re-link Payment Entries and guard an unpaid bill from silently becoming Paid. UI: the view screen now shows an Edit button for all five types, but only ESTIMATE (Quotation) has its screen wired to actually load and re-save the document. The other four route to their screen and the screen ignores the route option -- so their button currently does nothing useful.

Loading a document for edit resolves unit options and live stock SERVER-side (_edit_row_extras), reading Item/Bin directly instead of going through ERPNext's get_item_details(). get_item_details validates the item as if it were being sold right now, so any item retired from the catalogue since the document was made raised "Item X is disabled" -- once per affected line, as a dialog the user had to dismiss repeatedly (2026-08-29). Reopening is now one request for the whole document instead of one per line, which also removed 29 round-trips on a 29-line estimate.
expected_behavior: Every editable document type should reopen on the screen it was created on, with its own items loaded, and re-save through the amend path keeping its shop-facing number.
how_it_works: View a submitted document -> Edit -> screen reopens with the document's items -> add/remove/change -> Save -> original cancelled, correction submitted and chained, number carried forward.
how_to_use:
1. Open any saved Estimate from Sale > Estimate/Quotation (or a transaction row).
2. Click 'Edit Estimate'.
3. Add items, change qty or rate as needed.
4. Save -- the estimate number stays the same, the old version is kept cancelled as the audit trail.
qa_testing:
Verified 2026-08-29: all five doctypes rebuild correctly with items added and totals recalculated; Delivery Note stock verified exact (10 out, edited to 4, stock landed on start-4 -- no double deduction); ledger stayed balanced; repeated edits walk the amendment chain so passing an OLD document name still edits the LATEST version, leaving exactly one submitted document. Edge case found and fixed: an item DISABLED in the catalogue after the document was created used to break loading -- item_row threw and that row silently vanished from the reopened document. Both Estimate and Billing now fall back to the values stored on the document itself. Still to test: the four screens whose UI is not yet wired.

Regression to keep: reopen a document containing an item that is now disabled. Expected -- every line loads, no dialog, and the disabled line carries a `disabled` flag. Verified 2026-08-29 on a real 29-line estimate holding one retired item: 29/29 lines, all with unit options, zero dialogs.
related_features: Billing (POS), Sale Invoice (Edit Submitted), Items, Stock
if_we_modify:
Data impact: every edit creates a new docname (-1, -2...) and leaves the previous one cancelled forever -- that is the audit trail, never delete them. Stock impact: Delivery Note and Purchase Invoice edits reverse and repost stock; verify quantities land exactly, not doubled. Ledger impact: Purchase Invoice edits reverse and repost GL. Business logic impact: edit_submitted_document dispatches to each screen's own save_* function, so a change to any save_* function changes edit behaviour too -- they are deliberately the same path. Regression testing required: yes, per doctype, checking stock and ledger, not just that the document saved.

Loading rule: NEVER enrich a reopened document's rows through a sell-time API (get_item_details, get_sale_item_row or similar). Those validate against the catalogue's state TODAY, while a reopened document is a record of what happened THEN -- a disabled, renamed or price-changed item must still come back exactly as it was billed. Read Item/Bin directly and let anything unreadable degrade to a missing extra, never to a raised error.

description: The Home screen -- Total Receivable, Total Sale chart, Most Used Reports, and a right-hand rail of removable widget cards (Low Stocks Items and any others the shop adds).
what_it_does: Gives the owner a single at-a-glance view of money owed, sales trend, and shortcuts to the reports and screens used most often.
current_behavior: Widget cards in the right rail (.santu-dash-w-card) each carry a title, an optional period label, a value, and an absolutely-positioned remove (x) button pinned to the card's top-right. Until 2026-08-29 the header row reserved no space for that button, so the period text ran underneath it -- the Low Stocks widget rendered as 'As of No[x]'. Long period labels also wrapped onto a second line, changing the card's height. Both fixed: the row now reserves 30px on the right, the period never wraps, and the title takes the ellipsis when space runs out.
expected_behavior: A widget card's title, period and remove button should never touch each other, and the card should keep the same height whatever period label it carries.
how_it_works: Dashboard loads -> widget rail renders one card per configured widget -> each card shows title/period/value -> clicking the card opens the underlying screen, clicking x removes the widget from the rail.
how_to_use:
1. Open Home from the sidebar.
2. Read the summary cards and sales chart.
3. Use 'Add Widget of Your Choice' at the bottom of the right rail to add a widget, or the x on a card to remove one.
qa_testing:
Verified 2026-08-29 by measuring element boxes, not just by eye: remove-button vs period overlap = 0px, remove-button vs title overlap = 0px, across period labels 'As of Now', 'Yesterday', 'This Month', 'This Financial Year' and 'Last 12 Months', plus an artificially long widget title. Header row height stayed a constant 23px in every case (no wrapping).
Edge cases to re-check after any change here: the longest period label the app can produce, and the longest widget title -- the title is the element designed to truncate, the period is not.
if_we_modify:
UI impact: .santu-dash-w-remove is absolutely positioned, so ANY content added to .santu-dash-w-top must respect the 30px right padding or it will slide under the x button again -- this is exactly how the original bug happened.
Data/stock/ledger impact: none, presentation only.
Regression testing required: visual, but measure the boxes rather than eyeballing -- the overlap was small enough to miss at a glance and shipped unnoticed.

description: Hovering any icon button says what it does.
what_it_does: A single hover bubble explains icon-only controls across the whole app.
how_it_works: public/js/santu_tooltips.js listens once at the document level. Label order: data-tip, then title/aria-label, then a glyph map for icon-only buttons. A native title is moved onto data-tip once and permanently -- the first version stripped it on hover and restored it on mouseout, which lost labels for good whenever two hovers overlapped. Buttons whose face already spells a word are left alone.
how_to_use: Kisi bhi icon button par maus le jaayein -- neeche/upar chhoti si patti me uska matlab dikh jayega.
qa_testing: Hover every visible button on a screen and assert no icon-only button is left without a bubble. Billing: 15 icon buttons labelled, 0 orphans. Stock Summary and Parties: 0 orphans.
if_we_modify: Add new icon buttons with a title or data-tip, or add the glyph to the map in santu_tooltips.js. Do not mutate title on hover -- that was the bug.

description: Bill-CONTENT settings screen -- UPI ID for the Scan & Pay QR, plus the Thermal Invoice Library and WhatsApp/A4 Library template pickers. Separate on purpose from Printer Settings, which stays hardware-only (which printer, logo toggle, print density).
what_it_does: Lets the shop choose the UPI ID printed on every bill's QR, and which of the 11 thermal layouts / 6 A4 layouts is the default for each document type, with a live preview before committing.
current_behavior: santu_render_invoice_library() (in santu_printer_settings.js, loaded app-wide) renders both libraries with a shared live-preview pane. Printer Settings used to hold this same code (2026-08-29 direct request: 'invoice setting me thermal and a4 library dalna chahiye' -- template/layout choice is bill content, not printer hardware, so it moved out of Printer Settings into Invoice Settings, next to UPI ID). Printer Settings kept only Printer/Bill Header/Print Quality/Diagnostics after the split.
expected_behavior: A cashier or owner looking for 'which bill layout do we use' should find it next to the other bill-content setting (UPI ID), not buried inside printer hardware configuration.
how_it_works: Utilities > Invoice Settings -> set UPI ID and Save -> scroll to Thermal Invoice Library -> pick Document Type -> click a template card (live preview updates instantly) -> Set as Default -> that template is what actually prints/shares from now on. WhatsApp Library works the same way below it for A4 documents.
how_to_use:
1. Utilities > Invoice Settings.
2. Set UPI ID for the QR code, click Save.
3. Under Thermal Invoice Library, pick a Document Type, click any template card to preview it against a real recent document.
4. Click 'Set as Default' to make that template the one that actually prints.
5. Repeat for WhatsApp Library (A4 documents) below it.
qa_testing:
Verified 2026-08-29 after the move: Printer Settings no longer shows the library cards (hardware-only now); Invoice Settings shows UPI ID + both libraries + live preview; clicking a template card updates the preview instantly; Set as Default posts to the backend (200 OK) and the saved value was confirmed in Santu POS Settings.invoice_template_style; Test Print Template button (was at risk of being dropped in the split) confirmed present and wired to the shop's saved printer name.
Regression: full print/pricing suite re-run after the split, 343/343 pass -- the split did not change any print/PDF behavior, only which screen hosts the picker.
related_features: Printer Settings, Thermal Invoice Library, A4/WhatsApp Library, WhatsApp Connect
if_we_modify:
UI impact: santu_render_invoice_library() is shared code -- do not duplicate it into Printer Settings again; both screens load santu_printer_settings.js globally via hooks.py so the function is always available wherever it's called.
Printing impact: this IS the default-template picker for both thermal and A4 output -- any break here changes what every future bill actually looks like, silently, shop-wide.
Regression testing required: yes, re-verify Set as Default actually persists and that Printer Settings still works standalone (it now has no dependency on the library code at all).

description: Product catalogue -- every hardware/electrical/plumbing/paint item the shop stocks, with barcode, price, and stock unit.
what_it_does: Creates and maintains the master record every sale, purchase, and stock count is built on.
current_behavior: quick_create_item is the fast-add path used from 9 different callers across 7 screens (Billing, Sale Invoice, Purchase, Estimate, etc.) -- every item created here is forced is_stock_item=1 with a mandatory opening quantity on the selling side (require_opening_qty=0 is the one deliberate exemption, for Estimate/Quotation, which may quote goods not yet bought). This exists because items used to silently come out as non-stock Services when a cashier skipped the quantity field, invisible to stock counts forever after.
expected_behavior: An item should never be creatable in a state where it is invisible to stock tracking, except the one deliberate Estimate exemption.
how_it_works: Type a new item name where an item search comes up empty -> '+ Quick-create' -> name, price, unit, opening qty -> Item + opening Stock Entry created together.
how_to_use:
1. In any item search box, type a name that does not match an existing item.
2. Click '+ Quick-create <name>'.
3. Fill selling price, unit, opening quantity (how many are on the shelf right now).
4. Save -- item appears immediately in search, ready to sell.
qa_testing:
Normal: quick-create from Billing with a real opening qty.
Edge: opening qty of 0 on the selling side (must be blocked); creating from Estimate with no opening qty (must be allowed, stock shows 0).
Regression: since 9 different screens call this same function, a change here must be smoke-tested from at least Billing, Sale Invoice, and Estimate, not just one caller.
if_we_modify:
UI impact: 7 different screens' quick-add dialogs depend on this exact API contract -- changing a parameter name breaks all of them at once, not just one.
Stock impact: is_stock_item and the opening quantity guard are the two things standing between a real item and an invisible ghost item.

description: The mandatory foundational rules and architectural constraints for developing and modifying this application.
current_behavior:
This document acts as the absolute source of truth for AI agents and developers modifying the application.

**1. Project Memory - Mandatory**
- The Feature Workbook is the project's long-term memory.
- It must be continuously updated with requirements, bugs, edge cases, and business rules.
- Do not overwrite historical context unless obsolete.

**2. Inventory Unit Conversion - Critical Rule**
- Stock deduction MUST respect the actual selling unit.
- If an item is sold by feet (100 feet in stock, 1 foot sold), deduction is 1 foot. The system must NEVER deduct 1 meter instead.
- The system must never implicitly assume 1 foot = 1 meter.
- Conversion only happens when the item's explicitly configured UOM conversion requires it.

**3. Billing Identifier - Absolute Rule**
- NEVER start a billing flow/document with `SINV`.
- `SINV` must not be used as the starting identifier for any billing operation.
- Existing code using SINV-related logic must be reviewed and removed/replaced according to the POS billing architecture.

**4. Billing Screen Architecture**
- There is only ONE billing screen: **POS Billing**.
- Do not create duplicate screens for billing.
- Estimate, Challan, and other docs are separate workflows.

**5. Workflow Sequence**
- 1. Read Feature Workbook.
- 2. Inspect existing architecture.
- 3. Identify related features & past bugs.
- 4. Implement smallest correct change.
- 5. Test (including edge cases).
- 6. Update Feature Workbook.
- 7. Verify.

**6. Git - Source Control**
- Must push to Git.
- Never upload secrets, `.env`, or sensitive data.
- Ensure meaningful commits.
expected_behavior: Agents and developers must read this document BEFORE implementing any changes.

description: Creates a new Sales Invoice for a customer.
what_it_does: Allows the user to create a new POS/Sale invoice, add items, set quantities, collect payment, and generate a print/PDF/WhatsApp document.
current_behavior: Provides a full-screen POS UI or standard invoice form depending on settings. Updates stock and ledger upon save.
expected_behavior: Should quickly process a customer checkout with minimal clicks, updating inventory and accounts in real-time.
how_it_works:
User Action: Click 'Sale' -> Select Customer -> Scan/Select Items -> Enter Qty/Rate -> Collect Payment -> Save.
System Processing: Validates stock -> Creates Sales Invoice -> Creates Payment Entry -> Updates Bin (Stock) -> Updates GL Entry (Accounts).
Output: Prints thermal receipt / Sends WhatsApp.
how_to_use:
1. Go to Sales -> New Sale
2. Select Customer
3. Add items and update quantities
4. Select Payment Method (Cash/UPI)
5. Click Save
6. Invoice generated and stock updated.
qa_testing:
**Normal Scenario:** 5 items, exact cash payment.
**Edge Cases:**
- 0 items (should fail validation)
- 100+ items (should render fast and print correctly)
- Partial payment (should create outstanding balance)
- Negative stock (should warn or prevent based on settings)
if_we_modify:
**Impact Areas:**
- UI: Modifying item grid affects mobile and desktop POS.
- Data: Changes to Sales Invoice affect GL and Stock Ledger.
- Printing: Custom fields added here must be added to Print Formats.
**Regression Required:** Full checkout flow, partial payments, return flow.

description: Records money collected against a customer's outstanding balance, and the per-customer udhaar ceiling that blocks a sale from going too far over.
what_it_does: Payment In posts a real Payment Entry against one or more outstanding invoices. Credit Limit, editable from Parties > Edit Details, stops a NEW credit sale once the customer's total outstanding would cross the number set here.
current_behavior: _validate_credit_customer checks the limit before a credit sale is allowed to save; the message states the exact limit, what is already owed, what this bill adds, and the total that would result -- not ERPNext's generic 'contact your administrator' message. A cash sale, or a bypass_credit_limit_check row, is never blocked. Setting a limit below the customer's CURRENT outstanding is refused with a clear message rather than ERPNext's raw error.
expected_behavior: A credit limit is a business decision the shop owner (who IS the administrator here) makes directly from Parties -- it must never require going into a technical settings screen, and the block message must be something a 10th-pass-educated cashier can act on immediately.
how_it_works: Parties -> Edit Details -> set Udhaar Limit -> Save. Next credit sale to that customer: system totals existing outstanding + this bill's baaki; if it exceeds the limit, the sale is refused with the shortfall spelled out.
how_to_use:
1. Parties > pick customer > Edit Details.
2. Set 'Udhaar Limit (Credit Limit)'. Blank = no limit.
3. Save. The limit applies from the very next credit sale.
qa_testing:
Normal: sale within limit succeeds; sale exceeding limit is blocked with the correct numbers in the message.
Edge: limit set to 0 or blank (must mean no limit, not a limit of zero); cash sale must never be blocked regardless of limit; bypass flag must override the limit entirely; setting a limit below current outstanding must be refused with a clear message, not a raw ERPNext error.
Regression risk was fixed 2026-08-29 -- until then this feature was completely unusable because the limit could only be set once, at customer creation, and never edited afterward for any existing customer.
if_we_modify:
Business logic impact: touches the one function every credit sale in the app passes through -- test with a limit above, at, and below the sale amount.
UI impact: the Parties edit dialog is the only place this is settable; do not let a future edit remove that field again.

description: Goods returned to a supplier -- mirror of Sales Return on the buying side.
what_it_does: Reduces stock, reduces what the shop owes the supplier or records a refund actually received from the supplier.
current_behavior: Same pattern as Sales Return: save_purchase_return, settlement (credit vs refund) has no silent default, create_return_refund_payment posts a Receive-type Payment Entry when the supplier actually pays cash back.
expected_behavior: Same integrity requirement as Sales Return, mirrored for the supplier side.
how_it_works: Pick supplier/original purchase -> pick returned items -> pick settlement -> Save -> stock reduced -> return Purchase Invoice posted -> if refund, Payment Entry posted.
how_to_use:
1. Open Purchase Return, search the supplier or the original purchase bill.
2. Add returned item(s) and quantity.
3. Choose settlement (credit vs refund) -- mandatory, no default.
4. Save Return.
qa_testing:
Same scenarios as Sales Return, supplier side. Edge: returning more than was ever purchased.
Regression: verify stock never goes negative from an over-return.
related_features: Receive Stock, Supplier Ledger, Payment Out
if_we_modify: Same impact shape as Sales Return -- stock, ledger, and settlement default must all be re-verified together.

description: Corrects an already-submitted Sales Invoice by cancel + re-create, keeping the same bill number and any real payments already made.
what_it_does: Lets the shop fix a mistake on a bill that has already been submitted (wrong qty, wrong item, forgotten item) without touching accounting integrity.
current_behavior: edit_submitted_sale_invoice cancels the original ERPNext-natively (reverses GL, restores stock), then rebuilds a fresh invoice with amended_from pointing at the original -- the standard ERPNext amendment chain (name grows a -1, -2 suffix). santu_bill_no carries forward unchanged. A guard added 2026-08-29 stops an UNPAID bill from silently becoming marked Paid just because the edit screen prefilled the full amount as Amount Received (this genuinely happened to a real customer's bill and wiped their baaki to zero).
expected_behavior: Editing the goods on a credit bill must never change its payment status. A real payment collected mid-edit must be explicit (confirm_new_payment flag), never implicit.
how_it_works: Reopen invoice -> edit item/qty/rate -> Save -> original cancelled -> new invoice built with same bill number -> submitted -> stock and GL reflect only the corrected figures.
how_to_use:
1. Open the submitted Sale Invoice.
2. Use the edit action to reopen it for correction.
3. Change the item/qty/rate that was wrong.
4. Save -- the old bill is cancelled, a new one with the same bill number takes its place.
qa_testing:
Normal: correct a qty on a fully-paid cash bill; correct an item on an unpaid udhaar bill.
Edge: correcting a bill that already had a partial payment allocated against it (the payment must re-attach to the corrected invoice, not vanish).
Failure case (2026-08-28 real incident): editing an unpaid bill to add more goods silently marked it Paid, wiping Rs 5,476 of real customer debt -- root-caused and fixed; regression test must re-run this exact scenario every time this function changes.
Regression: verify Payment Entry References survive re-linking to the new invoice name.
related_features: Billing (POS), Customer Ledger, Payment In, Credit Limit
if_we_modify:
Data impact: creates a new Sales Invoice docname every edit (old one stays cancelled, permanent audit trail).
Ledger impact: GL fully reverses and reposts -- any bug here corrupts real financial history.
Stock impact: stock reverses and reposts for the corrected quantities.
Regression testing required: yes, always re-run the unpaid-bill-stays-unpaid scenario.

description: Customer returns goods against a past bill or with no bill at all; settles as khata credit or an actual cash/UPI refund.
what_it_does: Reduces stock back in, reduces or reverses the customer's amount owed, and records whether cash physically changed hands.
current_behavior: save_sales_return builds a return Sales Invoice (is_return=1, negative qty). "Paisa Kaise Settle Hoga" has NO default any more (fixed 2026-08-29) -- the cashier must explicitly pick Khata Credit or Refund Diya before Save Return is allowed; picking Refund calls create_return_refund_payment which posts a real Payment Entry (Pay, for a Sales Invoice return) so the customer's balance reflects reality immediately.
expected_behavior: A return where cash was genuinely handed back must never leave a phantom balance owed to the customer, and a return left as khata credit must never silently be treated as settled.
how_it_works: Pick customer/original bill -> pick returned items and quantities -> pick settlement (credit or refund) -> Save -> stock restored -> Sales Invoice (return) posted -> if refund, Payment Entry posted against it -> customer balance updates.
how_to_use:
1. Open Sales Return, search the customer or scan the original bill number.
2. Add the item(s) and quantity being returned.
3. Choose 'Khata me credit rahega' or 'Abhi cash/UPI refund diya' -- this field has no default, you must pick one.
4. Save Return.
qa_testing:
Normal: full return against a paid bill, partial return of one line from a multi-item bill.
Edge: return with no original bill (direct return), return quantity greater than what was ever sold (must be blocked or flagged), returning an already-cancelled invoice's items.
Failure case (2026-08-26 real incident): a real customer's cash refund was recorded as 'credit' by default, leaving a permanent -Rs110 phantom balance that only surfaced days later -- fixed by removing the default entirely.
Regression: always verify stock restoration quantity matches exactly, and that refund payments net the customer balance to the expected figure.
related_features: Billing (POS), Payment In, Customer Ledger, Credit Limit
if_we_modify:
UI impact: settlement choice must stay mandatory, never re-add a default.
Stock impact: return restores exact quantity to the exact warehouse.
Ledger impact: refund Payment Entry must debit the correct cash/bank account.
Regression testing required: yes -- this is the single highest-risk screen in the app for silent financial drift.

description: The fixed left navigation -- simple items (Home, Parties) and expandable parent groups (Sale, Return, WhatsApp, Utilities, Settings, More) with their child screens.
what_it_does: Primary navigation for the whole app, with the currently-open screen highlighted so the operator always knows where they are.
current_behavior: santu_fixed_sidebar.js builds two element shapes: a plain .santu-app-sidebar-item for leaf entries, and a .santu-app-sidebar-group wrapping a .santu-app-sidebar-parent button plus its children. Both get the same is-active class, but until 2026-08-29 they were styled very differently -- a leaf got the full red gradient plus a 3px red left accent bar, while an active PARENT got only a faint rgba(255,255,255,0.04) tint and no border. Selecting Home looked obviously active; selecting Sale or Utilities looked almost unselected. Both now share the identical active treatment.
expected_behavior: Whatever screen is open, its sidebar entry -- leaf or parent group -- should be highlighted with the same visual weight, so 'where am I' is never ambiguous.
how_it_works: Route changes -> sidebar re-evaluates each item's isActive() -> toggles is-active on the leaf item or on the group wrapper -> CSS paints the active row (red gradient background + red left accent + white bold text).
how_to_use: Click any sidebar entry. Parent groups expand to reveal their child screens; the parent stays highlighted while any of its children is open.
qa_testing:
Normal: open a leaf screen (Home) and a child screen under a parent (Billing under Sale) -- both the parent and the child row should read as active.
Edge: nested groups (Purchase & Expense inside More) must keep their extra indent while still showing the active style; collapsed sidebar mode has its own is-active rule that must stay in sync.
Regression after any sidebar CSS change: check at least one leaf route and one parent route side by side -- this exact mismatch went unnoticed for a long time because each looked fine in isolation.
related_features: Feature Workbook, Invoice Settings, Printer Settings, Billing (POS)
if_we_modify:
UI impact: .santu-app-sidebar-group.is-active > .santu-app-sidebar-parent and .santu-app-sidebar-item.is-active must be kept visually identical -- they are separate CSS rules, so a change to one silently diverges from the other.
Data/stock/ledger impact: none, this is presentation only.
Regression testing required: visual only, but check both a leaf route and a parent-group route, plus collapsed-sidebar mode.

description: 11 selectable thermal-roll bill layouts (Standard, Compact, Detailed, Simple Cash, Customer Copy, Duplicate/Office Copy, Bill+Payment Receipt, Delivery Slip, Large Print, Udhaar/Balance, Minimal Slip), each a genuinely different Print Format, chosen from Printer Settings.
what_it_does: Prints or previews a Sales Invoice as an ESC/POS-compatible thermal receipt sized to the actual paper width and to exactly how tall the bill needs to be -- no wasted blank roll, no clipped content.
current_behavior: Each template is its own real Print Format (Santu Thermal - <name>), not a query-string flag -- an earlier version tried to pass style= to one shared format and it silently did nothing, so all 'different' templates printed identically; that is fixed. Page height is estimated generously then the render is measured: if wkhtmltopdf paginated the content (meaning the estimate was too short and rows would be lost across the page break), the page height grows and it re-renders -- up to 3 attempts. The final PDF is then trimmed to the real content height plus an 8mm tail so the roll is not fed blank paper. Column widths were widened 2026-08-29 after a 100-item test found the '#' index column collided with the item name once numbering hit 3 digits ("100TEST ITEM 100").
expected_behavior: Every item on the invoice must appear on the printed thermal receipt, in order, with correct name/qty/rate/amount, regardless of how many items there are or how long the item names are, and with the minimum blank roll consumed.
how_it_works: Printer Settings > pick a template card -> live preview loads that exact Print Format via /printview -> Set as Default writes invoice_template_style on Santu POS Settings -> every future thermal print/PDF for Sales Invoice reads that setting and picks the matching Print Format automatically, falling back to the original Standard format if the chosen one is ever missing or invalid.
how_to_use:
1. Utilities > Printer Settings > Thermal Invoice Library.
2. Click any template card to preview it live against the most recent real invoice.
3. Click 'Set as Default' to make it the one that actually prints from now on.
qa_testing:
Verified 2026-08-29 with a real 100-line invoice across all 11 templates: every template rendered 100/100 items, correct numbering 1-100 continuous, no duplicates, item total matched the invoice grand total exactly. Edge cases covered: very long item names (14 in the test set) wrap instead of clipping; Large Print Bill and Detailed Bill (larger fonts/more columns) needed the auto-retry taller-page logic to avoid silently dropping items past a page break.
Regression: any change to a template's HTML/CSS must be re-tested with a 100-item bill, not just a normal 5-8 item one -- normal bills do not expose pagination bugs.
related_features: Billing (POS), WhatsApp Connect (image share), A4/WhatsApp Library
if_we_modify:
Printing impact: this is the literal printer output -- a broken template means a cashier hands a customer an incomplete bill with no error shown anywhere.
PDF impact: the same render path also produces the WhatsApp image/PDF -- a bug here is a bug in two channels at once.
Regression testing required: yes, with a large (100+) line-item bill specifically, not just a small one.

description: Speak to search for items in POS and Topbar.
what_it_does: Adds a microphone icon inside search bars. Clicking it activates speech recognition, listens to the voice (optimized for Indian accents), converts it to text, and automatically triggers the search.
how_to_use: Click the 🎤 icon in the POS search bar or Topbar transaction search, allow microphone permissions if asked, and speak the item name. The system will automatically type and search it.

description: In-app WhatsApp chat with customers -- send bills, estimates, payment reminders and balance statements directly from the shop's own WhatsApp number.
what_it_does: Shows a WhatsApp-style chat list of every customer/supplier with a phone number, lets the shop send a bill PDF/image, a payment reminder, or a free-text message without leaving the app.
current_behavior: Chat list comes from whatsapp_connect_api.get_chats. A 2026-08-29 bug meant the row for each contact was built but never appended to the visible list (list stayed empty even though the backend returned all contacts correctly) -- fixed with one missing $list.append(). Messages send through Santu WhatsApp Chat Message / Message Log records.
expected_behavior: Every customer/supplier with a phone number on file should appear in the chat list the moment the screen opens, most-recent-message first.
how_it_works: Open WhatsApp Connect -> contact list loads from every Customer/Supplier with a phone -> click a contact -> chat history loads -> Smart Messaging / Party Statement / Send Transactions / Payment Reminder buttons compose and send the relevant document as an image or PDF.
how_to_use:
1. Open WhatsApp from the left sidebar.
2. Click a contact, or search by name/phone.
3. Use the quick-action buttons (Smart Messaging, Party Statement, Send Transactions, Payment Reminder) or type a free message.
qa_testing:
Normal: contact list populates on load; opening a chat shows real prior messages and any past bill PDF.
Edge: a contact with zero prior messages ('Tap to open chat'); a very long chat history; a customer whose name has special characters.
Regression: after any edit to wa_connect_app.js, re-verify the contact list actually renders (this exact regression happened once already).
related_features: Customer Creation, Thermal Invoice Library, A4/WhatsApp Library, Payment In
if_we_modify:
UI impact: the render loop that builds each chat-list row must both build AND append the row -- easy to break silently since no error is thrown, the list just stays empty.
WhatsApp impact: this IS the WhatsApp integration; any break here is fully silent to the shop until someone notices no messages are going out.
